Article Title: ‘Few actors possessed his intensity’: PM Modi mourns Nana Patekar
Article Text:
Nana Patekar dies: PM Modi mourns veteran actor, hails ‘immense’ contribution to cinema

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday condoled veteran actor Nana Patekar , remembering his “immense” contribution to Hindi and Marathi cinema and praising his versatility and creativity.In a post on X, PM Modi wrote: “Few actors possessed the intensity, individuality and unmistakable presence that Shri Nana Patekar Ji had. He brought remarkable versatility and creativity to every role and gave us characters that will be remembered for generations. He was also admired for his frank and forthright views, never hesitating to express what he believed in.”He added: “Shri Nana Patekar’s contribution to Hindi and Marathi cinema was immense. His passing leaves a deep void. My condolences to his family, friends and countless admirers. Om Shanti.”While speaking at an event in Delhi, PM Modi remembered veteran actor.“This morning we got the news that the renowned actor Nana Patekar is no longer with us. He was an exceptional artist who won the hearts of audiences through a variety of roles,” PM Modi said.The Prime Minister said Patekar’s life was dedicated to the “honour and glory of the Tricolour” and used references to some of the actor’s well-known films to describe his career.“Nana Patekar’s life was dedicated to the honour and glory of the Tricolour. He refused to be bound by constraints; like a ‘Parinda’, he soared through the vast skies of cinema,” PM Modi said.He said Patekar used his films to raise questions about social issues and challenge the prevailing order.“Through his films, he launched scathing attacks on the prevailing societal order. He was a true Krantiveer who fought against social evils,” PM Modi said.PM also recalled Patekar’s distinctive screen presence, saying, “His silence was as impactful as his speech was powerful.”The Prime Minister said Patekar consistently spoke against anti-national elements and paid tribute to the actor while offering condolences to his family and admirers.“I pay tribute to Nana Patekar and offer my condolences to his family and admirers,” PM Modi said.Meanwhile, Union home minister Amit Shah also mourned Patekar, sharing a picture with the veteran actor and calling his passing an “irreparable loss” to the world of art.In a post, Shah wrote: “Over five decades, with his natural acting and powerful dialogue delivery, he left an indelible mark on the hearts of audiences. Whether it was serious social issues or humor-satire, he brought to life every character he portrayed. Through the 'Naam Foundation,' serving drought-stricken farmer families, or going to the border to boost the morale of soldiers, even after reaching the pinnacle of fame, he remained connected to his roots. ”He added: “Whenever I met him, his simplicity and straightforwardness always left a deep impression. May God grant strength to the grieving family and fans to bear this sorrow, and may the departed soul find a place at His divine feet.”Defence minister Rajnath Singh also paid tribute to Patekar, writing: “Nana Patekar was not merely an actor; he was an institution in himself. His remarkable contribution to Indian cinema will continue to inspire generations.”Patekar suffered a cardiac arrest at his home in Goa and was found unconscious. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead.Known for films including Prahaar, Parinda, Krantiveer, Tirangaa and Welcome, Patekar was one of the most recognised actors in Hindi and Marathi cinema.
Article Summary: PM Modi pays tribute to veteran actor, hails ‘immense’ contribution to cinema. Patekar suffered a cardiac arrest at his home in Goa and was found unconscious. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

Article Title: Make a good film, repay your debts: Supreme Court to Rajpal Yadav
Article Text:
File photo

NEW DELHI: Punishment and compassion may not mix in the justice delivery process, but they probably can walk together. Adopting this approach, Supreme Court Wednesday refused to relax the pre-condition of depositing Rs 2 crore for hearing the appeal of comedian Rajpal Yadav challenging his conviction and sentence of three months in a cheque bouncing case but suggested that he make a good film that would enable him to repay debts.A loan of Rs 5 crore he had taken in 2010 for producing the film 'Aata Pata Lapata', which remained on the verge of completion and never released because of litigation, spiralled into a huge sum with interest.A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalaya Bagchi and V Mohana assured senior advocate Ajit Kumar Sinha, who appeared for Muli Projects that had advanced the loan to Yadav, that it would ensure that the loan is repaid.Yadav was to deposit Rs 2 crore as a pre-condition for hearing of his appeal by Wednesday.Yadav's counsel Vikrant Yadav told the court that he has got a demand draft for Rs 1.15 crore and he has entered into an agreement with one Anand Prakash Yadav, who also was present in the court, to sell off his property. He sought time till Oct 13 to deposit the balance amount of Rs 85 lakh. SC agreed and protected him from surrendering to undergo jail term.The CJI said, "Make a good film and entertain people. You will be able to repay the loans." The apex court posted the case for hearing on Oct 15.
Article Summary: Comedian Rajpal Yadav was to deposit Rs 2 crore as a pre-condition for hearing of his appeal by Wednesday. Yadav is challenging his conviction and sentence of three months in a cheque bouncing case. A loan of Rs 5 crore he had taken in 2010 for producing the film 'Aata Pata Lapata' spiralled into a huge sum with interest.

Article Title: From 'vote chori' to 'chita andolan': Street protests return with a new playbook
Article Text:
Street protests are back, this time with new tools

During the INDIA bloc’s protest against the CEC, Priyanka Gandhi lay down on the road, daring anyone to move her.

The street has always been a political stage

How social media changed street mobilisation

Protest against CEC over SIR process in Delhi

When the youth lead, parties follow

Rahul Gandhi being taken away by police during a Congress protest against police action on demonstrators at Jantar Mantar.

Rahul Gandhi launched 'Satyagraha' website for information on current protests in India

Beyond Jantar Mantar: The protests away from the spotlight

Protest on women's sa​fety in Delhi

Protesters stage the 'Chita Andolan' in Madhya Pradesh's Panna district, demanding compensation and rehabilitation.

The street is old, the tools are changing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Slogans are ringing out, crowds are turning up and the streets are once again abuzz with protests.On Tuesday, INDIA bloc MPs took their protest against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to the national capital, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The march took an unexpected turn when Rahul Gandhi surprised the police with a last-minute change of course, turning it into a sit-in.A day later, opposition MPs were back with another dramatic flash protest on Janpath streets, where Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay down on the road and refused to budge until the CEC agreed to meet opposition leaders.And more could be coming. Cockroach Janata Party’s Abhijeet Dipke, who rallied young protesters during the anti-NEET paper leak agitation in July, has warned of a “Jantar Mantar 2.0” on October 10 if the CEC does not resign.But Delhi is not the only place, and politicians are not the only ones taking their grievances to the streets. Across the country, protests over very different issues are bringing people out in an attempt to make their voices heard.The protests differ in scale, issue and leadership. But together, they point to something familiar returning to the foreground: street politics.Peaceful protests have always been a part of our democracy.India's politics has rarely been confined to Parliament, party offices or election rallies. The streets have always had a part to play.Mahatma Gandhi turned marches, boycotts and satyagraha into instruments of mass politics during the freedom struggle. Decades later, Jayaprakash Narayan's movement drew students and citizens onto the streets against the Indira Gandhi government.Anna Hazare's anti-corruption protests filled Jantar Mantar and Ramlila Maidan in 2011. The anti-CAA protests saw prolonged sit-ins, while farmers camped at Delhi's borders for more than a year before the three farm laws were repealed.Street politics, then, is hardly new. What keeps changing are the tools used to trigger, spread and sustain mobilisation. Political analyst Uday Chandra feels social media is making protests more visible while also changing who can start and sustain them."Social media certainly makes protests visible to millions, enabling a rapid or viral spread. But it also does something more important: it reduces dependence on political parties, unions and established organisations to mobilise people. A grievance may now turn into a movement before conventional political actors decide how to respond," Uday Chandra says.But the current round of protests goes beyond social-media amplification, feels Chandra."I think something real is happening beyond social-media amplification. Street protest never quite disappeared from politics in India, but for much of the past decade, electoral politics under a highly centralised party machinery overshadowed it. What we are seeing now is, to my mind, the re-emergence of the street as an autonomous political arena," he said.What stands out in this round of protests is not just the issues being raised, but who is often raising them first.On questions ranging from examinations to electoral rolls, young people have managed to create pressure outside the usual party machinery. Increasingly, political parties have found themselves responding aggressively to issues they did not start.So, have young people and students shown political parties the way back to street mobilisation? The events surrounding the NEET protests in July this year are a case in point.As students protested over the paper leak, Jantar Mantar became the centre of an agitation that continued for weeks. The CJP emerged as the pressure group leading the agitation and eventually ensuring the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.Many political parties that initially stood on the sidelines scrambled to join the agitation. On July 21, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Mallikarjun Kharge and other opposition leaders staged a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence over police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak.But Chandra argues that the CJP, as a movement, differs significantly from political parties and earlier large movements such as the Anna Hazare agitation or the farmers' protests."CJP is much more decentralised than the two movements you mention. The Anna movement had recognisable leaders and a national campaign/agenda. Likewise, the farmers’ protests rested on strong unions, local organisation, and the economic capacity to sustain mobilisation for months. By contrast, what we see emerging now is networked, relatively leader-light, and often issue-specific," he said.The CJP advantage is also organisational, he feels."Instagram, WhatsApp, YouTube and other online platforms can connect previously unrelated groups rapidly. Mobilisation is, therefore, not only faster but more fluid. You do not necessarily need to build and register an organisation before launching a movement. Increasingly, the movement precedes the organisation," Chandra adds.It is perhaps this realisation that has forced political parties to course-correct their mobilisation strategies.Rahul Gandhi, who faced criticism for prioritising his "Chhatron ki Goonj" campaign instead of backing the anti-NEET protests led by CJP, has now made a more direct attempt to help Congress enter the protest space. On October 4, he launched the 'Satyagraha' portal, which seeks to map protests across the country and connect people agitating over different issues.For Chandra, the move shows that Congress has recognised the risks of ignoring protests that begin online and then spill onto the streets."The Satyagraha platform strikes me as an attempt to situate the INC within an emerging ecology of anti-BJP protests. This is an interesting shift in political organisation. It takes the party from a traditional top-heavy high command structure to a node connecting diverse and dispersed struggles against the status quo."The high-decibel protests against Gyanesh Kumar or over NEET are only one part of the story, perhaps the more visible one. Away from the national spotlight, peaceful protests have been taking place across the country over a wide range of issues.They may be small, localised and often unconnected: women’s safety, land, displacement, water, facilities in schools, local governance and more. But together, they show how the street remains an important space for people trying to make themselves heard.In Delhi, young women have marched over women's safety after cases of sexual violence. Demonstrations have also spread to cities including Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Ahmedabad, Patna and Dehradun, with protesters demanding safer public spaces and greater accountability from governments and police.In Madhya Pradesh’s Panna district, families affected by the Ken-Betwa river-linking project have revived their "Chita Andolan". Protesters have slept on funeral pyres, stood in water and gone on hunger strike over compensation and rehabilitation.In Maharashtra’s Maval, farmers opposing the Pavana closed pipeline project announced a 'jal samadhi' agitation while also demanding rehabilitation for families that surrendered land for the Pavana dam decades ago.Water has also brought farmers onto the streets in Karnataka, where organisations in Krishna basin districts have opposed releasing reservoir water to Telangana, arguing that drought-hit areas within Karnataka should be given priority.At IIT Bombay too, students have turned their protest over the death by suicide of student Sahil Wakode into a hunger strike, with the JNU Students’ Union joining calls for action on the demands raised by protesters.The scale and demands vary sharply. Some protests involve thousands; others are confined to a university campus, a few villages or even a handful of streets. They may target the Centre, state governments, local administrations or institutions, but the impulse is the same: take the grievance to the street.So, street politics is old, but the mobilisation techniques have changed. Earlier movements depended heavily on student organisations, unions, public meetings and, later, television coverage. Today, a protest can begin on Instagram or X before it reaches Jantar Mantar.Social media has also changed the language of protest. A slogan shouted on the street can become a meme within hours, while posters, one-liners, chants and songs travel far beyond the protest site.Recent demonstrations have offered plenty of examples. At women's protests in Delhi, slogans such as 'Ek kachori, do samosa, in mardon ka kya bharosa' quickly travelled from the street to Instagram reels, using humour and rhyme to make a serious point about women's safety and gender attitudes.At the Mumbai protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, placards carried lines such as 'Gyanu must go' and the Bollywood-inspired 'Vote churaya mera, kisne o sanam? Gyanu ne'. Days later, Rahul Gandhi carried the Gen Z-style message "Gyanesh, it's done bro!" during the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission. Whether it will culiminate into effective but what it definitely did was make people stop and notice.And Gen Z may not be the youngest generation learning to protest.In Lucknow, around 200 schoolgirls blocked a road in the rain over a shortage of teachers and a damaged road leading to their school. In Fatehpur, around 1,000 students staged a four-hour protest demanding drinking water and repairs to classrooms. In several cases, authorities acted after the protests.What has changed is not the instinct to protest, but how quickly a grievance can find an audience and become visible. The slogan may now become a meme and the mobilisation may begin on a phone screen. The destination, however, is often still the same: the street.
Article Summary: Street protests are back, this time with new tools. Priyanka Gandhi lay down on the road, daring anyone to move her. The street has always been a political stage. But the tools used to trigger, spread and sustain mobilisation are changing.

Article Title: 'We'll do it': PM Modi gives slogan for 2047 goals; credits people’s support for 25-year unbroken run
Article Text:
PM Modi said the Indian economy was considered a ‘gone case’ when he took office in 2014, and the picture has completely changed now

Target unprecedented and extraordinary goals: Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi chose the milestone of his unbroken run of 25 years as head of govt on Wednesday to deliver a message imbued with optimism and passion for achieving the target of developed India by 2047, crediting people's support for his feat and asking citizens to join him in dedicating themselves to the ambitious goal."We will do it," Modi said at a BJP event, a clarion call which repeatedly punctuated his one-hour-long address and what, he said, has guided him in setting his goals, since he became Gujarat CM in 2001 with no administrative experience, and achieve them with support of "janshakti" (people's power)."Karma is my dharma. When I took oath as Gujarat CM, I never thought such an occasion will come," he said at Viksit Bharat Sankalp Sabha, asking people to take a pledge to put the nation first and not stop till India becomes a developed country. His speech came amid the opposition's high-decibel protest in the heart of the city over the SIR row but he appeared unfazed.Modi’s speech on his 25 years as head of govt came amid the opposition’s protest in Delhi over the SIR row, but he did not join the issue, except for a sideswipe at his rivals when he said a big tragedy for the country had been that it was divided for votes due to political expedience.Water crisis in agriculture or power shortage does not hit any particular caste or community, Modi said.“When a problem troubles everyone, then the solution too should cover everyone,” he said, adding this was why his govt linked good governance and saturation to inclusion.Reiteration of his “tireless” resolve to make India a leading player in a gamut of sectors, including tourism, education, sports, entertainment and science, ran through the nearly hour-long speech as its central theme.“Our pilot (Smit Machchhar) is being discussed globally today. Made-in-India planes will be discussed tomorrow... It will be an injustice to the country if we set small and easy goals. We should target unprecedented and extraordinary goals,” Modi said.“Viksit Bharat by 2047: we will do it. Top three economy: we will do it. Self-reliant: we will do it,” he said.Addressing the criticism that his target of “Viksit Bharat by 2047” is too far into the future, he said the idea of an independent India two decades before 1947 had looked improbable. India has 140 crore citizens now as against less than 40 crore then and is much more capable, he said.Modi said the Indian economy was considered a “gone case” when he took office in 2014, and the picture had completely changed now.Lauding RSS volunteers and BJP members, he recalled his rise from a humble background, saying he was always driven by a desire to learn. “No incident was a waste for me. Those who helped me win taught me humility. Those who brought me down taught me to stand up. Those who opposed me taught me the power of democracy. Every crisis was a test of my patience,” he said.Modi said he was never driven by ambition but mission, adding he never intended to contest elections and was busy helping others fight polls as a senior organisational functionary in BJP before being asked to take over as Gujarat CM.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi chose the milestone of his unbroken run of 25 years as head of govt to deliver a message imbued with optimism and passion for achieving the target of developed India by 2047. His speech came amid the opposition's high- decibel protest in the heart of the city over the SIR row but he appeared unfazed.

NEW DELHI: The Air Force on Thursday marked its 94th Air Force Day with a ceremonial parade and display of its key combat assets at Hindan airbase, with Air chief marshal AP Singh highlighting the force's preparedness and the importance of air power in modern conflicts.Speaking at the event, Air chief Singh said the IAF remained prepared to deal with any challenge and pointed to its performance during Operation Sindoor “We are alert, ready to meet any challenges; IAF showed speed of combat operation during Operation Sindoor,” the Air Chief said.He said recent conflicts around the world had underlined the growing importance of air power in protecting a country’s interests.“Conflicts in parts of world have shown air power is primary means of protecting interests of a nation,” Singh said.The Air Chief, who is set to retire on October 31, also reflected on his tenure and called it a matter of pride to have led the force.“Proud moment for me; serving as IAF chief was my biggest fortune,” Singh said.The celebrations began with a ceremonial parade at the Hindan air base. The three service chiefs, senior military officials and several former IAF chiefs attended the event.Singh arrived at the parade venue in a vintage car from the 1960s, while three helicopters flew past in a ‘Dhwaj’ formation.The IAF also put several of its frontline aircraft, helicopters, weapons and air defence systems on static display. These included Rafale, Su-30 MKI and Jaguar fighter jets, along with LCH Prachand and ALH Dhruv helicopters.Critical weapon and air defence systems were also showcased as part of the celebrations.

Article Title: Pakistan's terror monsters now wreak havoc in its own backyard: India at UN
Article Text:
‘You cannot run with the hares’: India tears into Pakistan’s terror record at UN

Pakistan’s own leaders expose terror threat

‘Bombed-out airfields’ are not victory

'Circular economy of words'

‘The victims in Pahalgam were not asked about their political orientation’

India raises Masood Azhar issue

India invokes 9/11, 26/11 and Pahalgam

Stronger international cooperation Action against terror networks Better intelligence sharing Stronger measures against terror financing 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: India used the UN stage to turn Pakistan’s own words against it, arguing that the terror networks Islamabad once nurtured have now come back to haunt their own backyard, a reality, New Delhi said, that even Pakistan’s leaders have begun to acknowledge. India also urged the international community to take stronger action against states accused of sponsoring terrorism.Speaking at the UN General Assembly’s Sixth Committee, which deals with legal affairs, India’s first secretary Raghoo Puri said Pakistan had long portrayed itself as both a victim and a frontline state in the fight against terrorism."Pakistan has presented itself as a frontline state in combating terrorism and as a victim, while masking the fact that the Frankenstein’s (monster) the Pakistani state has created and lost control over have moved from wreaking havoc in neighbouring countries to doing the same in Pakistan," Puri said on Wednesday."This was exposed recently by a provincial chief minister of Pakistan, and may I jog the memory of colleagues to an interview in 2018 by her father and former prime minister of Pakistan, exposing this dark secret," he said."You cannot run with the hares and hunt with the hounds," Puri warned. "Reality never works like that".Puri was responding to remarks by Pakistan’s deputy Permanent Representative Usman Jadoon, who had launched an attack on India during the committee proceedings.Puri pointed to recent remarks by Punjab chief minister Maryam Nawaz , who said her province faced a bigger threat from neighbouring Pakistani provinces than from neighbouring countries.Maryam Nawaz, who leads Pakistan’s Punjab province, said last month in Lahore: "Unfortunately, the threat Punjab, a province of 130 million, faces comes less from my neighbouring countries and more from my neighbouring provinces."Earlier this month, she also questioned the idea of distinguishing between different forms of extremist violence, saying anyone involved in terrorism should be treated as a terrorist regardless of their political motives.Puri also referred to an interview given by Maryam Nawaz’s father, former Pakistan prime minister Nawaz Sharif, to Dawn in 2018. Sharif had spoken about militant groups operating from Pakistan and questioned whether they should be allowed to cross the border and carry out attacks in India."Militant organisations are active. Call them non-state actors; should we allow them to cross the border and kill 150 people in Mumbai?" he had said.Puri did not name either Maryam Nawaz or Nawaz Sharif while making his remarks.Puri also hit back at Pakistan’s claims about the outcome of Operation Sindoor , India’s counterterror military action to the Pahalgam attack."If bombed-out airfields and cratered runways look like victory to Pakistan, they are, of course, welcome to enjoy it," he said.He accused Pakistan of continuing to spread false claims about the operation and said its approach was part of a wider campaign of disinformation.Puri said the "Pakistani representative’s desperation to falsely tout the Pakistani military’s narrative on the outcome of Operation Sindoor" was consistent with Pakistan’s long-running use of state-backed misinformation and psychological warfare.Puri also took a swipe at Pakistan after its delegation made a second intervention, repeating what he described as old arguments."Pakistan believes in the circular economy of words and narratives," Puri said."If this much effort had actually been made in countering terrorism rather than narrative building, misinformation, and disinformation, the world would have been a better place," he said."But nothing more can be expected from a Form 47 government," he added, referring to Pakistan’s political system and alleged manipulation of the electoral process.Puri also challenged Pakistan’s claims on minority rights and accused Islamabad of allowing religious extremism to flourish."The victims in Pahalgam were not asked about their political orientation; they were asked about their religion," Puri said."It is therefore deeply ironic that Pakistan speaks of combating religious hatred while allowing the conditions that enable it to persist and thrive, especially by fomenting cross-border terrorism," he added.Puri referred to the Pahalgam terror attack, in which terrorists targeted tourists after asking about their religion.He said the attack showed the consequences of allowing extremist groups and crossborder terrorism to continue.Puri also questioned Pakistan’s claims that it was taking action against Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar, who is listed by the UN as a terrorist.Pakistan had increased the reward for information leading to Azhar’s arrest from Pakistani rupees 50 lakh to 70 lakh."Pakistan glosses over its state support for terrorism by announcing enhanced rewards for apprehending UN-listed head of Jaish-e-Mohammed, terrorist and mastermind of several attacks against my country," Puri said."When the media can reach Masood Azhar and get confirmation from him about the success of Operation Sindoor, surely the Pakistani state knows his whereabouts," he said.Azhar had earlier appeared in a video in which he claimed that his family infrastructure had been destroyed during India’s strikes on Bahawalpur as part of Operation Sindoor.Puri also recalled Pakistan’s earlier claims that Jaish-e-Mohammed was no longer active."Just a few months ago, Pakistani representatives used this forum to call the Jaish-e-Mohammed a defunct organisation," Puri said. "The world has seen the script play earlier, and we are clear-eyed that this time also it is going to be no different."Puri warned that allowing terrorist groups to operate with political protection could undermine international efforts against terrorism."When terrorist groups are allowed to operate under state political power, international commitments become meaningless, and when perpetrators are provided safe havens, the victims of terrorism are denied justice," he said.He also cited the example of al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden, who was found in Abbottabad, Pakistan, years after the 9/11 attacks."The world has not forgotten 9/11, and where its perpetrators, including Osama bin Laden, were caught," Puri said.He then pointed to the 2008 Mumbai attacks."The world has not forgotten 26/11," when Pakistani terrorists killed 166 people in Mumbai, he said. "The world has not forgotten Pahalgam."Puri also referred to Pakistan’s record on terror financing and the upcoming meeting of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF)."The world is aware of Pakistan’s financial support to terrorism, as also, the FATF plenary meeting coming up soon," he said.The FATF, the global body that monitors terror financing and money laundering, is scheduled to hold its next plenary meeting in Paris from October 26 to 30.
Article Summary: Pakistan has long portrayed itself as both a victim and a frontline state in the fight against terrorism, India's first secretary Raghoo Puri said. Puri was responding to remarks by Pakistan’s deputy Permanent Representative Usman Jadoon, who had launched an attack on India during the committee proceedings.

Article Title: Can a picture make healthy food irresistible to teens?
Article Text:
Even without any single “problem” food, simply eating a very large meal is one of the strongest triggers. Holiday dinners, big restaurant plates, or second helpings that push the meal into the heavy category regularly led to that classic “food coma.”

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A bowl of millet porridge may not sound as tempting as a burger, but put it through a social-media makeover and teenagers may look at it differently. An Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN) study involving 203 adolescents found that the visual appeal of food images was significantly associated with their willingness to consume the food.Researchers showed adolescents attractive “foodporn” images of healthy foods on Instagram for 15 days and compared them with regular images. The strongest differences were seen for millet porridge and boiled chana salad, whose attractive images generated about 50% and 10% more positive responses, respectively, than their regular counterparts. The difference was statistically significant for the millet and pulse categories.The study used 15 food images divided into three categories: unhealthy foods presented as “foodporn”, healthy foods presented in an attractive “foodporn” format, and healthy foods shown as regular pictures. The researchers also conducted in-depth interviews with 19 adolescents to understand what made food images appealing.Researchers found that the intervention showed a broader positive trend, with adolescents reporting more favourable attitudes towards healthy foods, greater consumption and stronger intentions to eat them, although not all changes were statistically significant.Intentions to consume millet porridge and chana salad were 9% and 15% higher, respectively, for attractive images than regular ones, but neither difference was statistically significant.Visual appeal appeared important, with adolescents citing colour, presentation, ingredients, angle, texture, glossiness, balance and symmetry as factors that made food images more appealing. Even before the intervention, 60% said they were willing to try foods seen on social media, while 56% said attractive food images made them crave them.Adding nutritional information did not significantly alter responses, suggesting that adolescents paid more attention to the visual presentation than accompanying text.The findings suggest that making healthy foods visually appealing could help counter the dominance of attractive unhealthy-food content online, with potential applications in school canteens, restaurants and cafes. However, the study did not establish that attractive food images change actual eating behaviour. The intervention was short, relied partly on self-reported responses, and could not establish causality.
Article Summary: Researchers showed adolescents attractive “foodporn’ images of healthy foods on Instagram for 15 days and compared them with regular images. The strongest differences were seen for millet porridge and boiled chana salad, whose attractive images generated about 50% and 10% more positive responses, respectively.

Article Title: Anti-CEC protests: Opposition, police face off again; Rahul Gandhi says won’t stop till Gyanesh quits

NEW DELHI: Opposition INDIA bloc members on Wednesday travelled by buses from their lunch meeting in Connaught Place towards Jantar Mantar, seeking to protest and demand CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. But for the second day in a row, Delhi Police stalled their agitation, detaining them less than 1km from their intended “flash protest” site.“We are not going to stop protesting till CEC Gyanesh Kumar resigns,” said Rahul Gandhi , who was detained along with 90 others, including MPs and workers, after hours of confrontation with police in front of Shangri-La hotel. They were taken to Barakhamba police station and released later around 8:30 pm.Later, Congress issued a directive to all its state, block and district committees, to hold “massive demonstrations” to protest the police action to prevent the INDIA bloc from holding a protest at Jantar Mantar. “Congress declares today as a black day for Indian democracy,” it stated.The joint opposition made it clear that their protest will continue undeterred and a bigger protest plan is in the works for Thursday.However, Delhi Police said restrictions imposed under BNSS’s Section 163 were in force in the New Delhi area, which is why the protesters were detained. “As Section 163 is in force here… protest marches or demonstrations are not allowed without permission,” DCP Sachin Sharma said.It all began with Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge hosting INDIA bloc MPs for lunch at a restaurant in Janpath, which began around 1.30pm and where the gathering was informed about a plan to continue the protest against CEC, this time with a march to Jantar Mantar for a demonstration.Members, including Congress’s Rahul, KC Venugopal and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, John Brittas (CPM), P Sandosh Kumar (CPI), Manoj Jha (RJD), Derek O’Brien (TMC), Thol Thirumavalavan (VCK), emerged from the restaurant and announced the protest plan. MPs of JMM and IUML also joined them.They headed for buses waiting for them to leave. But the administration had stationed police in heavy numbers at Janpath, which, coupled with the gathering of onlookers and rush of political workers, made it difficult for the buses to move. Some Congress MPs and functionaries climbed on the roof of one of the buses, waving Tricolour. The MPs were forced to dismount from the buses in front of the hotel, where they were surrounded by police. Priyanka, Raja Warring and Deepender Hooda sat down on the road along with some workers, even as the cops continued to request Rahul to get into a bus. Cops finally picked up Rahul and took him away in a mini van. Similarly, Priyanka, who was lying on the street clutching a copy of the Constitution, along with other women workers of her party, was removed.Police claimed that some protesters attacked their personnel. A sub-inspector alleged protesters bit him and tore his uniform. Police are also analysing mobile-phone videos following allegations that police personnel, including women, were assaulted near Jantar Mantar.Kharge and Rahul said the opposition will continue with its protests till CEC resigns. On an FIR being registered against him for entering Akashvani Bhavan premises and staging an eight-hour sit-in Tuesday, Rahul said, “I have 45 FIRs against me. Left and TMC functionaries were also dismissive of any lingering differences.
Article Summary: Opposition INDIA bloc members on Wednesday travelled by buses from their lunch meeting in Connaught Place towards Jantar Mantar. But for the second day in a row, Delhi Police stalled their agitation, detaining them less than 1km from their intended ‘flash protest’ site.

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already generated enormous excitement around Indian cricket , but former India captain Kapil Dev believes it is far too early to judge whether the teenage sensation can go on to become the next big name in the game.At 15, Sooryavanshi has already made a significant impact at the age-group, India A, IPL and is now part of India’s T20I setup. But with the youngster currently waiting for his opportunity behind the established opening pair of Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson, Kapil believes there is little value in rushing to make predictions about his future.“It’s too early. Does he have the ability? Yes. But there have been so many in cricket who came with so much ability, then faded out,” Kapil told Times of India.Kapil cited former India batter Vinod Kambli as an example of a player whose immense talent did not translate into the kind of long-term career many expected.“Look at Vinod Kambli. What we will say about that?” he said.Sooryavanshi, who is still only 15, has plenty of time on his side. Kapil believes the next few years will be more revealing than his current performances.“Vaibhav is 15 years old. Give him another three years, then we will talk.When his lifestyle changes, his thinking too will change. Then we’ll come to know how he will look after the next two years. That is more important than looking at his performance,” Kapil said.The teenager has already given Indian cricket plenty to talk about. In June, in his last innings as an uncapped player, Sooryavanshi smashed the fastest fifty in List A cricket, reaching the milestone in just 11 balls before finishing with 94 off 29 balls for India A in the tri-series final against Sri Lanka A.Earlier in February, he produced another remarkable performance in the Under-19 World Cup final in Harare, smashing 175 off 80 balls to help India Under-19 win the title. His IPL career also began with a bang, In 2026 season he broke several batting records this year and won the Orange Cap before being blooded into India’s T20I side.But Kapil’s broader view of young cricketers is not about one innings or one season. Those type of cricketers. We have seen Rohit, Virat. We already saw Sachin. And they made us so proud,” Kapil told Times of India.“But you’re always looking for the next hero. You always ask, ‘Who is the next hero?’ As a cricketer I like to see which is that young boy who has got that chance, who can replace Virat Kohli . And play for 15 years. That’s what my mind looks for.”For Sooryavanshi, the attention is unlikely to disappear anytime soon. But Kapil’s message is clear: talent can open the door, but how a teenager develops away from the spotlight may ultimately determine how long he stays at the top.

Article Title: Patrick Mahomes' $504.75 million contract still leaves him nearly $490 million behind Tom Brady's $650 million fortune
Article Text:
Tom Brady vs Patrick Mahomes net worth 2026 (Getty Images)

How does Mahomes' $504.75 million contract compare with Tom Brady's $650 million fortune?

tom brady and patrick mahomes (Getty Images)

What did Tom Brady actually earn in 23 NFL seasons?

Why did retirement make Tom Brady richer than his playing days?

## What does Mahomes own away from the field?

Can Patrick Mahomes ever catch Tom Brady's fortune?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patrick Mahomes signed an eight-year, $504.75 million deal with the Kansas City Chiefs in June 2026, yet his estimated net worth sits at $160 million. Tom Brady, retired since 2023, is valued at $650 million. That leaves a gap of roughly $490 million, close to half a billion dollars. Those are Celebrity Net Worth estimates, not audited accounts. Timing, ownership stakes and a Fox Sports contract explain most of the difference. Brady built his fortune over 23 seasons and a second career in broadcasting. Mahomes is only in his 10th season.A contract is not a bank balance, and that is where most of the confusion starts. Mahomes' $504.75 million is spread across eight seasons, 2026 through 2033. He collects $56.75 million in cash this year, rising to $70 million in the final season. Only $150 million was fully guaranteed at signing. Incentives could lift the total to $522.25 million, but none of that arrives in one payment.Put the contract next to Brady's $650 million and the gap is about $145 million, not half a billion. The big number appears when you compare net worths instead. Mahomes sits at $160 million.Brady sits at $650 million. The spread is $490 million.So why does a $504.75 million deal translate to a $160 million fortune? Because most of it has not been paid. Celebrity Net Worth tracks about $289 million in career cash for Mahomes through this season. Taxes, fees and spending come out of that, so a net worth well below career earnings is normal.About $333 million in salary. That number surprises people. Brady made roughly $230 million of it across 20 years in New England, often by restructuring deals so the Patriots had cap room. He earned around $28.3 million in 2020, $39.4 million in 2021 and about $30 million in 2022 with Tampa Bay. Endorsements added well over $100 million. Salary and sponsors together passed $450 million before taxes.Here is the twist. Mahomes is on pace to pass Brady's entire career salary by the end of next season. Celebrity Net Worth's projections put his cumulative cash at $346.75 million after 2027, which clears Brady's $333 million. Brady needed 23 years. Mahomes needs 11, and he will do it while still in his early thirties.Because the largest gains came after the last snap. Fox signed Brady in 2022 to a 10-year, $375 million contract, an average of $37.5 million a year. He skipped the 2023 season, debuted in the booth in September 2024 and is back for a third year. If the money is paid evenly, his first two seasons are worth roughly $75 million. That deal alone could out-earn his 23 years of playing salary.The bigger driver is the Raiders. NFL owners approved Brady's 5% stake in October 2024. He and partner Tom Wagner paid $220 million for a combined 10%, so Brady's share cost about $110 million before fees, or roughly $122 million with his half of an extra $24 million in fees. In May 2026, a deal for more than 25% of the team valued the Raiders at about $9.9 billion. At a round $10 billion, Brady's slice is worth around $500 million on paper.That single asset is worth more than three times Mahomes' entire net worth. It comes with caveats. The stake is private, non-controlling and hard to sell, so $500 million is a benchmark, not a payout. Not every bet worked, either. His FTX shares were wiped out when the exchange collapsed in November 2022.Brady also has a say in how the team is run. He has described his role as strategic advisory and works with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick in the 2026 draft. Owning a team while calling games for Fox also limits his access to opposing teams.Quite a lot. He holds minority stakes in the Kansas City Royals, bought in August 2020, and in Sporting Kansas City. His wife, Brittany, was a founding investor in the NWSL's Kansas City Current, and Patrick later joined that ownership group. In 2023 he and Travis Kelce joined investors who bought into the Alpine Formula 1 team.The catch is that none of the purchase prices or stake sizes were disclosed. That leaves estimators guessing, so his $160 million is harder to pin down than Brady's Raiders figure, which has real numbers behind it. Add endorsements from Adidas, State Farm, Oakley, T-Mobile, Hy-Vee and others, and his off-field income is already substantial.The contract runs through 2033, when Mahomes will be 38. If he collects all of his scheduled base pay, career cash would approach $737 million before endorsements. Kansas City reworked the deal in 2023, restructured it again early in 2026 and rewrote it in June, and Celebrity Net Worth expects another revisit before it expires.Health is the variable nobody can price. Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL in December 2025, in a season that ended with Kansas City at 6-11 and out of the playoffs for the first time in his career as a starter. He was cleared for training camp in July and said in August the knee felt strong.The real lesson from Brady's climb is that equity has done more than salary. One of his most valuable assets is a Raiders stake that cost about $110 million. Mahomes will collect $56.75 million this year and a scheduled $58 million in 2027, which adds up to $114.75 million in cash. That is already more than Brady paid for the stake that now anchors his fortune.
Article Summary: Patrick Mahomes signed an eight-year, $504.75 million deal with the Kansas City Chiefs. His estimated net worth sits at $160 million. Tom Brady, retired since 2023, is valued at $650 million. Timing, ownership stakes and a Fox Sports contract explain most of the difference.

Article Title: 'Pain on left side': Nana Patekar's late-night message and what doctors revealed about the hours that followed

After a local television report highlighted the effort, another $2,100 came in, taking the total to“We sold enough mugs to raise $2,000 [in 2023],” Stowe told PEOPLE.The money went through Stowe’s Out of the Red Friday initiative, which focuses on paying off school lunch debt.The fundraiser came at a time when school meal debt remained a serious issue for families across the United States. Stowe’s project offered a direct way for customers to contribute while buying a handmade item tied to one of football’s best-known families.The campaign also reflected Donna’s willingness to share something personal for a cause involving children. Her cookie recipe had already become part of the Kelce family's public story after she became widely recognised for making the treats for Travis and Jason.Donna previously described the recipe as something especially meaningful to her.“I’m like, ‘What has my life become?’”She also explained why she hoped others would make the cookies themselves:“It’s an absolute favorite for me and everyone in the family” and that she hopes other people “will enjoy them as much as we have through the years and gather in the kitchen with their own families and friends to bake them, just as I do with mine.”For Stowe, the next step was potentially delivering the funds directly to schools with Donna. She said she had invited Kelce to join her, although the Super Bowl schedule made the timing difficult.The fundraiser showed how a simple family recipe could take on a second life. In this case, every mug sold helped turn Donna Kelce’s famous cookies into support for children who needed help with school meals.
Article Summary: Donna Kelce's famous chocolate chip cookie recipe helped raise $4,100. A local business owner received permission from the mother of NFL stars Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce to place the recipe on handmade mugs. Part of every sale went towards school meal debt.

'I am working just as hard on my bowling'

Naman Dhir made a strong statement on his T20I debut against the West Indies, and his performance has already led to questions about Washington Sundar ’s place in India’s white-ball teams.The 25-year-old, who has mainly been seen as a batting all-rounder in the IPL, surprised many with the ball in the first T20I. He bowled his full four-over spell and returned figures of 3/31 as India restricted the West Indies to 171.Dhir had scored 318 runs in IPL 2026 but did not bowl a single over during the tournament. His international debut showed that he can offer India another option with the ball.Former India cricketer and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth believes Dhir’s emergence could seriously hurt Washington Sundar’s chances in white-ball cricket.Srikkanth pointed out that Dhir initially came into the team as a replacement but has now made it difficult for the selectors to leave him out."Naman Dhir has now come in at Washington Sundar's place as a replacement player. Washington Sundar keeps getting injured after every two matches. Now Naman Dhir has come in as his replacement and finished him. How can you drop Naman Dhir now from ODIs and T20Is? He has immediately grabbed that spot.Now Washington Sundar can only play for India in Test cricket," Srikkanth said on his YouTube channel.Srikkanth was also impressed by how Dhir adjusted his bowling after getting hit."When he bowls fast, he gets hit for sixes. So he immediately slows the ball down, which shows that he's a very thoughtful bowler. He's ideal for T20 cricket. He bowls in such a way that he envisions himself batting and how one would bowl to him. That's how much of a thinking cricketer he looks to be. That's why he's an intelligent bowler."Dhir’s performance also made Srikkanth question the impact of the IPL’s Impact Player rule."This is why the Impact Player rule should be removed in the IPL. That's how you'll produce genuine all-rounders. Now you've got a good batting all-rounder in Naman Dhir. Today he bowled four overs, but even if he gives you two overs on a consistent basis, it'll be huge for India and MI," said Srikkanth.Srikkanth expects Dhir to get more opportunities with the ball in the IPL as well."He'll take loads of wickets even in the upcoming IPL. He must have bowled only 10 overs maximum in his IPL career, yet he bowled four overs today. He has everything, including luck."Dhir, however, made it clear that his bowling was not something he suddenly picked up for his international debut.“I have been bowling for quite some time; it is not as if I have just started now. In the IPL, because of the impact-player rule, you don’t see me bowling as much. But it is not that I haven’t bowled. I have bowled a lot and have good experience here as well. Hopefully, I will continue doing well in the future,” Dhir said in the post-match press conference after helping India bowl out West Indies for 171 in the first T20I here.He explained that he followed a simple plan after watching Axar Patel bowl earlier in the innings.“I saw Axar Bhai bowling earlier, and he was bowling a little slower and getting some turn. That was in my mind - if I bowled a little slower, there would be good grip from the wicket, and I could get them out. So I just stuck to my plans and kept things basic. I think I got a good result from that," Dhir said.Dhir also stressed that his bowling has always received the same attention as his batting.“Again, I will say that even if you haven’t seen me bowling, I have been bowling as much as I have since I came here and I have practised just as much before this. It is not as if, as a batting all-rounder or bowling all-rounder, I have neglected one aspect. Yes, my batting is a plus point, but at the same time I am working just as hard on my bowling,” he said.“Whether I have to bowl four overs, two overs or even one-day cricket, where I have bowled six or seven overs, it is normal for me. I just have to focus on my plans and try to execute them,” he added.India, who won the three-match ODI series 2-1, are leading the five-match T20I series 1-0.The second T20I match will be playd on Friday at the JSCA International Stadium Complex in Ranchi.

Founded by Travis Kelce in 2015, 87 & Running Foundation aims to empower underserved youth by providing resources and opportunities in education, athletics, STEM, and the arts. Its “Ignition Lab” collaboration with the nonprofit organization Operation Breaththrough reflects the foundation’s mission.Through the Ignition Lab program, under-resourced teenagers from Kansas City neighborhoods can explore STEM and entrepreneurship with mentorship, equipment, and hands-on learning.Although 87 & Running Foundation’s Instagram account has seen no recent activity, its charitable work continues through initiatives like Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab.According to the foundation’s website, the Ignition Lab program serves about 700 students daily. Young people have opportunities to learn, create, develop practical skills, and explore several pathways that could shape their future education and careers.87 & Running Foundation’s official Instagram account has not posted any content since January 2026. At the same time, social media fans raised money-laundering allegations against the foundation.According to The Arizona Republic, the foundation’s IRS filings reported raising about $1.5 million and spending roughly $1.1 million over a multi-year period [2021 to 2024].Only 41 cents of every dollar was reportedly directed to charitable programs.A substantial share of spending was classified as management and general expenses, including payments to A&A Management Group.Travis Kelce’s longtime business managers, twin brothers Aaron and Andre Eanes, co-founded A&A Management Group. The firm is closely associated with the tight end’s outside-gridiron business operations.CharityWatch executive director, Laurie Styron, told The Arizona Republic that, “players and their managers need to stop using charities this way. Don’t get creative. Don’t look for loopholes.If you establish a charity, stop mixing in business interests or using friends to operate it. Do it the right way or don’t do it at all. There are a lot of ways for players to give back without founding their own charity.”Despite this growing tension, Travis Kelce’s foundation reportedly continued its work through the Ignition Lab program with Operation Breakthrough. Operation Breakthrough is a nonprofit organization that provides educational and developmental opportunities for children and families in Kansas City.Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation funds and powers its Ignition Lab program. The program gives 14- to 18-year-old teenagers access to resources that promote innovation, technical learning, and entrepreneurial thinking. This partnership expands 87 & Running Foundation’s financial support to create opportunities for young people.In August 2026, Operation Breakthrough expressed heartfelt gratitude to Travis Kelce for arranging an opportunity for Ignition Lab students. The students attended the Kansas City Chiefs’ first preseason game from Kelce’s suite at Arrowhead Stadium.The organization wrote on Instagram, “Talk about a suit surprise! Thanks to Travis Kelce, our Ignition Lab students experienced the Chiefs’ first preseason game from his suite at Arrowhead!”The post also mentioned that the students met Travis Kelce’s mother, Donna Kelce, during the outing. This experience gave participating students a heartfelt opportunity to enjoy a Chiefs game. It also helped them create lasting memories connected to their Kansas City community.The 87 & Running Foundation’s 2025 annual report speaks for the foundation’s continued charitable work.Their website also provides information about its programs and partnerships. However, their collaboration with Operation Breakthrough through Ignition Lat provides additional insight into the foundation's activities and its connection to the Kelce family. In particular, Travis Kelce’s father, Ed Kelce.On September 17, 2026, Operation Breakthrough shared a post on Instagram about Ed Kelce visiting. The father of NFL legends Jason and Travis Kelce read to first-grade students and showed them the cutest, rarest childhood photos of Jason and Travis.The organization wrote, “Storytime with a side of Kelce family throwbacks! Ed Kelce stopped by to read to our first graders, then gave them a peek at Travis and Jason when they were little, just like them! Thank you, Ed, for sharing your time and a little family history with our children!”Yesterday, it was Travis Kelce’s 37th birthday on October 5, 2026. The little angels at Operation Breakthrough sent warmest wishes for the Kansas City Chiefs tight end through an adorable Instagram reel.The organization collaborated on the post with 87 & Running Foundation and called it, “Little voices, BIG birthday wishes! Happy birthday, Travis! Sending lots of love from all of us at Operation Breakthrough.” This post marks the 87 & Running Foundation’s first social media update since January 2026.
Article Summary: 87 & Running Foundation aims to empower underserved youth by providing resources and opportunities in education, athletics, STEM, and the arts. Its “Ignition Lab” collaboration with the nonprofit organization Operation Breaththrough reflects the foundation’s mission.Through the Ignition Lab program, under- resourced teenagers from Kansas City neighborhoods can explore STEM and entrepreneurship.

The Kansas City Current are preparing for a much bigger future at CPKC Stadium, and the latest move could reshape the club’s place in women’s soccer. Kansas City has approved $185 million in public funding for the stadium expansion, paving the way for thousands of new seats and major improvements around the Riverfront. For co-owners Patrick and Brittany Mahomes , the project adds another major chapter to a club they have helped build from the ground up. The expansion also strengthens Kansas City’s bid to attract major international sporting events and turn the Riverfront into an even bigger destination for fans.The Mahomes connection to the Kansas City Current goes beyond Patrick’s profile as the Chiefs’ star quarterback. Brittany Mahomes was part of the original ownership group that brought the NWSL franchise to Kansas City, while Patrick joined the ownership team in 2023. The Current officially lists both as co-owners, alongside Angie Long and Chris Long.That gives the stadium expansion added significance for the Mahomes family. CPKC Stadium opened in 2024 with 11,500 seats and quickly became a major symbol of the growth of women’s professional sports. Now, the proposed work would increase capacity to 18,000.The plan calls for about 6,500 additional seats, mainly in the corners between the existing grandstands.The club also intends to raise the roofline, add more premium boxes and double its suite capacity.For a team that has already attracted strong crowds, the larger venue could give the Current more room to build its audience while creating additional opportunities for premium hospitality and major events.The stadium project is part of a much larger transformation of the Berkley Riverfront area. The broader $1.4 billion development is expected to bring new housing, retail, parking and infrastructure improvements, creating a district designed to remain active beyond match days.The Current also sees the expanded stadium as a potential gateway to major international events. Kansas City is looking ahead to opportunities such as the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup and the Men’s Rugby World Cup, making venue capacity and facilities increasingly important.There is also a financial safeguard attached to the public funding. The team and its development partners have committed to covering the city’s bond debt if tax revenue does not generate enough money to meet those payments.Construction on the stadium expansion is expected to begin after next season. If completed as planned, CPKC Stadium will offer the Current a significantly larger stage while helping reshape Kansas City’s Riverfront into a year-round sports and entertainment destination.

Article Title: Why did Jon Rahm quit LIV Golf? Reason behind $300 million star’s departure explained
Article Text:
Jon Rahm quits LIV Golf. Image via: Richard Heathcote/ Getty Images

Why did Jon Rahm quit LIV Golf?

What does Rahm's exit mean for LIV Golf and his next move?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jon Rahm is leaving LIV Golf. His lawyer, John Beck, told a New Jersey bankruptcy judge on Wednesday that the Spaniard reviewed the terms of the league's restructured version, called LIV 2.0, and found them unacceptable. Rahm signed in December 2023 and has won the league's season title three years running. The two-time major champion won't be part of the rebuilt tour, and both sides are working on a separation agreement. Money looks like the core issue, though neither has spelled out the terms.Jon Rahm signed as the reigning Masters champion on a deal reported at more than $300 million. He won four LIV events, but the paychecks are where the trouble sits. LIV filed for Chapter 11 protection on Sept. 8, listing between $500 million and $1 billion in liabilities. Rahm tops the league's list of 30 largest unsecured claims at $7.5 million in past-due payments. He had also said he had no regrets about joining and wanted the league to be sustainable.The second version of the league looks nothing like the first. CEO Scott O'Neil has described 10 events with smaller purses, and said the league has to move away from a Saudi-style plan toward one that stands on its own.A proposed $300 million investment from BC Partners depends on conditions that include new player agreements. Nobody is forced to sign one. Players have no obligation to join LIV 2.0, even with multiyear deals on the books.Beck told the court the terms were "unacceptable as to him." No figures came with the statement. In May, Rahm had said he saw few ways out of a contract with several years left. The bankruptcy has since changed his circumstances, and it was later said both camps are in advanced talks on a consensual separation.The PGA Tour door looks shut. CEO Brian Rolapp said on Sept. 15 that the tour has no plans to bring back the Returning Member Program, the route Brooks Koepka used to rejoin. Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith were the other names it could have covered.The DP World Tour is the other path. Rahm settled his dispute with the European circuit in May, which kept his membership and his Ryder Cup eligibility for next year. Where he plays in 2027 is not settled.The $300 million star has a thin major record since the move. He has one top-five and four top-10 finishes at majors, after three top-10s in 2023 alone.LIV has its own problems. Sergio Garcia has been released from his contract, and the deadline for current players to commit now sits at Oct. 25. It is not clear which players BC Partners requires for the deal to close, so Rahm's absence adds to the uncertainty. Following his departure, DeChambeau is the biggest name left on the roster.
Article Summary: Masters champion Jon Rahm is leaving LIV Golf. LIV filed for Chapter 11 protection on Sept. 8, listing between $500 million and $1 billion in liabilities. Rahm tops the league's list of 30 largest unsecured claims at $7.5 million in past-due payments.

Article Title: Candace Parker finally reveals Caitlin Clark’s heated playoff moment after the Fever star screamed at the WNBA legend

Caitlin Clark. Image via: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images

What did Caitlin Clark yell at Candace Parker?

How much did WNBA playoff viewership drop after the Fever lost?

Caitlin Clark hit a big three against the Aces, turned toward the scorer's table, and screamed at Candace Parker. The WNBA legend was sitting there minding her own business. Parker has now explained what she heard, and the answer includes a pointed question and one swear word that cannot be printed here. She went through it on Wednesday's Post Moves podcast, which she co-hosts with Clark's Fever teammate Aaliyah Boston, and kept things light with a Steph Curry comparison. Las Vegas won the first-round series 2-1 and eliminated the Fever.Candace Parker was telling the story to Aaliyah Boston. She was at the scorer's table, she said, when Clark knocked down the three and turned on her. Parker was unsure of the exact words, so she tried two versions out loud. Did Clark ask what she thought this was, or did a curse word sit in the middle of the question?Parker went with the second. Boston, laughing, confirmed it. Parker's own reaction was simple. She wanted to say great shot, keep things moving, and go back to sitting there.The pair had already settled it in person. After the game, cameras appeared to catch the Fever point guard telling Parker, "I blacked out," and both laughed it off.Parker gave the moment some context. She pointed to a night years ago when Curry hit a shot and walked over to Reggie Miller, who was calling the game, to say something.Same energy, she said, and she found it cool. The three-time Finals champion added that she wanted opponents to do exactly this when she played. She asked for the trash talk and the finger in her face because it fired her up. Some players feed off chaos, in Parker's view, and she used to be one of them.Her verdict on Clark's outburst was short.The Fever's exit set off a ratings argument almost right away. A post on X claimed the playoffs lost 70 to 76 percent of their viewers once Clark was gone. It had no source and passed a million views in about 18 hours. Other accounts pushed the figure as high as 78 percent.The fairer comparison is Game 1 of Fever-Aces against the two Game 1s of the semifinals, played Sunday. USA Today reporter Christine Brennan posted the numbers: 2.11 million viewers for Fever-Aces on ABC, 1.17 million for Liberty-Dream on ABC, and 1.12 million for Aces-Valkyries on NBC and Peacock. Front Office Sports reporter Colin Salao shared the same figures. By that math, the drop is 44 to 47 percent.It is still a big fall, but it is well short of the viral claims. Each semifinal opener still pulled more than a million viewers, and four teams are chasing the title.
Article Summary: Caitlin Clark hit a big three against the Aces, turned toward the scorer's table, and screamed at Candace Parker. Parker has now explained what she heard, and the answer includes a pointed question and one swear word. Clark appeared to catch the Fever point guard telling Parker, "I blacked out"

Kentucky community rallies around Neven Coofer’s family

A Kentucky baseball community is mourning the sudden loss of 6-year-old Neven Coofer, a young Little League player remembered for his kindness, energy and love for his older brother. Neven died unexpectedly in his sleep on Oct. 1, leaving his family, teammates and friends struggling to understand the loss. His family is still waiting for an official cause of death. In the days since, people across Lexington have come together to remember a boy whose presence brought joy to those around him. A community fundraiser is also helping his family manage the difficult days ahead.Neven began playing baseball at age four in the Southeastern Cal Ripken Baseball League. Though he was still very young, league officials said he quickly became one of the most familiar faces at the ballpark.Aaron Anderkin, vice president of the league, described the impression Neven made on everyone around him.“If you had to think of one six-year-old at this park that everyone knew, that they gravitated towards, that just had an infectious personality, it was Neven.”His family remembers that warmth in equally personal terms.Neven’s mother, Gordana Coofer, said her son was full of happiness and described him in words that captured the depth of her loss.“Neven was everything that was good in this world,” his mom, Gordana Coofer told Fox 56, adding that she remembered her son as “happy.”His father, Dominick Coofer, also spoke about the close bond Neven shared with his 8-year-old brother, Niko. Neven often watched his brother play baseball, taking photos and videos on his iPad.“He’s his brother’s biggest cheerleader,” his father, Dominick Coofer, told the outlet about Neven’s older brother, Niko, 8. “There’s pictures of him with his iPad getting pictures of his brother and videos of his brother playing baseball.”The family said Neven had a history of febrile seizures and had been diagnosed with Kawasaki disease, an inflammatory condition that can affect blood vessels and, in some cases, the heart. However, no official cause of death has been announced.His death has also brought an outpouring of memories from people who knew him. Niko returned to the baseball field on Oct. 5, stepping up to the plate in his brother’s memory.“If you were sad, he would come up to you and ask if you were okay,” Niko said.A GoFundMe campaign has since been created to support the Coofer family as they navigate the financial and emotional weight of their loss. The fundraiser describes Neven as a child who brought “so much light, love, and joy” to those around him.For a community that watched him grow through baseball, his absence is difficult to put into words. Yet the stories being shared about Neven show how deeply a six-year-old boy touched the people around him.
Article Summary: Neven Coofer, 6, died unexpectedly in his sleep on Oct. 1. His family is still waiting for an official cause of death.
